parameters.quote: Manufacturers must report any battery-related fire, thermal runaway, or other incident involving injury, property damage, evacuation, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported within 5 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a material safety risk requiring action; otherwise, include relevant incident trends in the next scheduled safety notice.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers must report any battery-related fire, thermal runaway, or other incident involving injury, property damage, evacuation, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported within 5 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a material safety risk requiring action; otherwise, include relevant incident trends in the next scheduled safety notice.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report any battery-related fire, thermal runaway, or other incident involving injury, property damage, evacuation, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported within 5 business days. Reports must include known unit/model and incident details, with updates as facts are confirmed. Within 30 days of adoption, manufacturers must also report to the relevant regulator any known thermal incidents from the prior 12 months that were not previously reported. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a material safety risk requiring action; otherwise, include relevant incident trends in the next scheduled safety notice. Reporting is required even when the cause is not yet known.

parameters.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative samples before initial sale, after a material model change, and at least annually. Manufacturers must provide results, including sample size and failure rate, to the relevant regulator and to customers who buy that model; per-model results need not be published publicly. A failure rate above 5% requires a corrective-action plan and interim risk controls submitted to the regulator within 30 days, followed by remediation and retesting within 12 months.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative samples before initial sale, after a material model change, and at least annually. Manufacturers must provide results, including sample size and failure rate, to the relevant regulator and to customers who buy that model; per-model results need not be published publicly. A failure rate above 5% requires a corrective-action plan and interim risk controls submitted to the regulator within 30 days, followed by remediation and retesting within 12 months.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative samples before initial sale, after a material model change, and at least annually. Manufacturers must provide results, including sample size and failure rate, to the relevant regulator and to customers who buy that model; per-model results need not be published publicly. A failure rate above 5% requires a corrective-action plan and interim risk controls submitted to the regulator within 30 days, followed by remediation and retesting within 12 months. Existing models may remain on sale during that period subject to regulator oversight and any interim restrictions the regulator considers necessary. At retest, a model above 5% may not be offered for sale until it meets the maximum. New models must meet the 5% maximum before initial sale. Follow-up results must be provided to the regulator and affected customers.

parameters.quote: All new units must support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear customer instructions. Manufacturers must provide a plan to enable the capability on compatible installed units, and complete deployment within 72 months of adoption. Where a unit cannot be upgraded, the manufacturer must notify its owner and the relevant regulator and provide an equivalent safety measure or replacement plan.

parameters.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption. The suppression system must be appropriate to the unit’s battery chemistry and validated not to create additional hazards.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption. The suppression system must be appropriate to the unit’s battery chemistry and validated not to create additional hazards.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption. The suppression system must be appropriate to the unit’s battery chemistry and validated not to create additional hazards. Manufacturers must document its performance and maintenance requirements and provide them to customers and the relevant regulator.

parameters.quote: Notify affected customers promptly when a material safety risk requires action, and provide updates as information changes. A manufacturer must initiate a mandatory recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: Notify affected customers promptly when a material safety risk requires action, and provide updates as information changes. A manufacturer must initiate a mandatory recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must provide customers clear safety notices for their model, including known hazards, safe installation and use, maintenance, and any action customers should take. Notify affected customers promptly when a material safety risk requires action, and provide updates as information changes. A manufacturer must initiate a mandatory recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Regulators may also require a recall where incident evidence indicates an imminent or otherwise material safety risk.

judge_section_notes: The final rules are a balanced compromise: S2 adopts Halcyon's 5% thermal-test maximum with a 12-month remediation window for existing models, while S5 adopts Northwind's 8/100k mandatory recall trigger, which catches Halcyon's Ember 8. Northwind secures a 72-month remote-shutoff retrofit deadline and avoids public per-model failure-rate disclosure; Halcyon secures customer access to per-model results and a 36-month lead time for built-in fire suppression. S1 is strict on reporting, including reporting while cause is unknown.
